title: [Demo] Nanosweeper.lol: Minesweeper backed by real Nano transactions
author: cbrunnkvist
selftext:
**Title:**  
I've been working on [Nanosweeper.lol](https://dev.nanosweeper.lol/), a browser-based Minesweeper game where **every move produces a real Nano mainnet transaction**. Yeah this ain’t on Bitcoin or some Ethereum clone… Because we need real speed, and no fees. And no dumb “smart contracts” :-)

I had a fairly clear CQRS-shaped model of how I wanted the client and server to interact before implementation, and have been using Codex (Plus) extensively to bring it to life. 

The server applies moves after transaction confirmation, with live updates, and we also have spectator mode and replays and (budding) analytics. 

It's still a “beta”, but I've recently improved confirmation times, error recovery and mobile layout, and added chording. Also, it has a pixel-art mine sniffing rat and a hardhat-wearing hamster. Not animated. Yet.

Ask me in comments for some XNO dust in case any of the faucets give you trouble. Or you can just watch [a replay](https://dev.nanosweeper.lol/proof-of-play/ae2f5fbb21d53f3c201572fe2fb38ed7296e13980ec0012dcb6a8e5e3d0f99d9#rewatch) to get a feeling of how it plays, first. 

AI was used extensively for coding. The architecture, game loop and UI direction were mine.

I'd be interested in hearing how other AI-assisted developers tackle debugging and reliability across systems with asynchronous events and shared state. 

I’ve added Sentry.io because there’s some WebGPU shenanigans I have to deal with, and RUM is the only way unfortunately …
